title: Tate twists are well defined and locally free of rank one
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\cO_E$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $X$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ be the sheaf of
$\ell^n$th roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], with transition maps
$\mu_{\ell^{n+1},X}\to\mu_{\ell^n,X}$, $u\mapsto u^\ell$. For every finite commutative ring $A$ and integer $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, write $A_X$ for its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $A_X(1)=\mu_{\ell^r,X}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_X}A_X$, with sheaf tensor as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Interpret the coefficient objects and twists for $\cO_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$ using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

1. There is a pro-étale cover $\widetilde X\to X$ and a compatible system
   $(\zeta_n)_{n\ge1}$, $\zeta_n\in\mu_{\ell^n,X}(\widetilde X)$, $\zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$,
   such that each $\zeta_n$ generates: $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_{\widetilde X}\to\mu_{\ell^n,\widetilde X}$,
   $a\mapsto\zeta_n^a$, is an isomorphism.
2. For $r'\ge r$, the Kummer map
   $\mu_{\ell^{r'},X}\to\mu_{\ell^r,X}$, $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{r'-r}}$, induces an isomorphism
   $\mu_{\ell^{r'},X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^{r'}}A_X\cong\mu_{\ell^r,X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_X$;
   so $A_X(1)$ is independent of $r$ up to canonical isomorphism.
3. For $\Lambda\in\{A,\cO_E,E,\Qlb\}$, the sheaf $\Lambda_X(1)$ is an invertible
   $\Lambda_X$-module: on $\widetilde X$ it is isomorphic to $\Lambda_{\widetilde X}$. Hence
   so are $\Lambda_X(d)$ and $\Lambda_X(-d)$ for $d\ge0$, and
   $\Lambda_X(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(-d)\cong\Lambda_X$. The functor $K\mapsto K(d)$ is an autoequivalence, with inverse $K\mapsto K(-d)$, on each coefficient category defined in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]: $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ and the bounded constructible categories for $\cO_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$.

proof.text: Use the existing local root-tower model to choose one pro-etale covering family with compatible generators and compatible integral root bases. Convert the generators to the stated residue-linear bases and prove the Kummer transition composition, identity, and generator formulas by the actual exponent maps.

Define the finite Kummer map by scalar extension of the root transition. The adjunct pure-tensor formula is exactly the required formula. On each member of the chosen root cover, conjugate by the extended bases: the map sends the basis generator to the basis generator, so it is an isomorphism there and hence globally. The same bases trivialize the finite line.

SignedLineTensorEquivalence gives signed line bases and opposite tensor evaluations. Derive its exact tensor functors on unbounded complexes and identify the degree-zero tensor model, obtaining the specified finite inverse functors.

The root-cover integral extension basis trivializes each integral first line; signed line equivalence gives all its signed powers. Identify each ordinary finite reduction with the finite signed line using the scalar-extension tensor comparison and the existing integral local models. Apply integral line reduction/restriction and cancel the fully faithful inclusion to identify the restricted inverse pair with the actual intrinsic integral twist functors.

Localize the integral inverse pair and its tensor comparison. Tensor-induction on coefficient morphisms identifies the localized tensor with the prescribed rational tensor; exactness and coefficient linearity give the rational inverse pair. Good line representatives and the completed tensor comparison give opposite integral object products, and localization gives the rational products.

For local rational signed lines, use the generic completed object-pullback calculation on each integral signed line and its slice basis; transport through the actual rational pullback object specification. Embed the rational line and product at the least coefficient field. The normalized same-stage scalar and tensor comparisons identify its image with the specified algebraically closed line and tensor product.

At algebraically closed coefficients use natural fixed-right tensor associativity, the regular unit, and the already proved opposite line products to build the two inverse functor isomorphisms. The normalized braiding gives the reversed product. These isomorphisms give an equivalence by CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk. Assemble every clause using the same root covering family.
